concepts.label: DMA cache maintenance

concepts.definition: Keeping some mixture-of-experts weights in host memory or storage and fetching the experts a batch needs into accelerator memory, often prefetching predicted ones, which lets a model larger than accelerator memory run at the cost of transfers.
concepts.label: Expert offloading

concepts.definition: Choosing, for each training step, sequence or context parallel degrees and how packed documents are sharded across ranks from that step's sequence lengths and attention patterns, so ranks receive balanced attention work.
concepts.label: Variable-length parallelism planning

concepts.definition: Scheduling co-located workloads on one accelerator in small units of a kernel, so latency-sensitive work can preempt background work quickly and interference stays bounded.
concepts.label: Fine-grained accelerator sharing

concepts.definition: Scheduling generative-inference operations with complementary compute, memory, or communication demands concurrently on one accelerator, using small batches or fused kernels so several hardware resources stay busy together.
concepts.label: Intra-device overlap of bottlenecks

concepts.definition: Pipeline parallelism that partitions a model whose layers form a branching graph into stages that follow the graph, so independent branches, such as separate modality encoders, run concurrently in parallel stages instead of being serialized into one chain.
concepts.label: Graph pipeline parallelism

concepts.definition: Coordinating the retrieval and generation work of retrieval-augmented requests across requests and processors, overlapping and batching work across the stage boundary and optionally adapting retrieval settings per query, to meet latency and answer-quality targets.
concepts.label: RAG pipeline scheduling

concepts.definition: Profiling that correlates timestamped events and calling contexts from model code, frameworks, native libraries, and accelerator kernels, so that device time and stalls can be attributed to the operations that launched them.
concepts.label: Cross-stack profiling

concepts.definition: Keeping some models' weights resident in accelerator memory and loading others from host memory or storage on demand, so a shared accelerator serves more models than fit at once, at the cost of transfer latency.
concepts.label: Model swapping and residency

concepts.definition: Laying out and allocating accelerator memory for cached attention state, which trades fragmentation and sharing against kernel compatibility and allocation cost.
concepts.label: KV-cache memory allocation

concepts.definition: The per-position subnetwork of learned projections and a nonlinearity paired with attention in each Transformer block, which in most architectures holds the largest share of a dense model's parameters, executes as large matrix multiplications, and is the sublayer that mixture-of-experts routing replaces.
concepts.label: Feed-forward block

concepts.definition: A contract binding a provider to stated service targets, with declared consequences such as credits or penalties when they are missed, whose targets are usually set looser than the internal objectives that trigger engineering response.
concepts.label: Service-level agreement

concepts.definition: Delay imposed on short or ready work because a queue serves in arrival order and a long or stalled item ahead holds the service point, so an item's wait depends on what is in front of it rather than on its own cost.
concepts.label: Head-of-line blocking

concepts.definition: A distinction between arrivals scheduled independently of responses and arrivals triggered by prior completions, which changes offered-load feedback and the queueing behavior a load test exposes.
concepts.label: Open-loop vs. closed-loop load

concepts.definition: A collective in which every participant ends with the same reduction, usually the sum, of all participants' equal-shaped tensors, the operation that synchronizes gradients across replicas in data-parallel training.
concepts.label: All-reduce

concepts.definition: The complementary collectives in which each participant receives one reduced shard of the group's tensors (reduce-scatter) or the concatenation of every participant's shard (all-gather), the pair that moves sharded parameters and gradients in fully sharded training and composes into a bandwidth-optimal all-reduce.
concepts.label: Reduce-scatter and all-gather

concepts.definition: A fabric in which accelerator nodes form a multidimensional grid with wraparound links to fixed neighbors rather than tiers of switches, so neighbor and ring traffic can run at link rate while global exchanges are routed hop by hop with lower bisection bandwidth that depends on dimensions, routing, and contention.
concepts.label: Torus topology

concepts.definition: Provisioning less uplink capacity at a switch tier than the downlink capacity it serves, written as a downlink-to-uplink ratio, which cuts fabric cost but makes cross-tier bandwidth contend when many endpoints communicate at once, as synchronized collectives do.
concepts.label: Network oversubscription

concepts.definition: Memory directly managed by the host processor and used for input staging or offloaded model state, whose capacity and accelerator access costs depend on the platform's memory and interconnect design.
concepts.label: Host memory tier

concepts.definition: A compiler design in which what an operator computes is written once and how it runs, meaning loop order, tiling, vectorization, unrolling, memory placement, and parallel mapping, is a separate composable schedule, so the same algorithm can be retargeted and tuned without changing its semantics.
concepts.label: Algorithm-schedule separation

concepts.definition: The barriers, memory fences, and atomic read-modify-write operations through which threads of a kernel coordinate access to shared data, where barrier stalls and contended atomics serialize work that the thread hierarchy otherwise runs in parallel.
concepts.label: Kernel synchronization and atomics

concepts.definition: The maximum distance over which a link meets its signal-quality requirements for a specified medium and signaling scheme, constraining cabling, retiming, and the geometry of connected accelerator domains.
concepts.label: Link reach limit (copper versus optics)

concepts.definition: Whether a workload reads storage in large contiguous ranges or in many small scattered requests, which decides whether sequential throughput or per-request latency and IOPS bound it, and so which media, layout, and shard sizes suit it.
concepts.label: Sequential versus random storage access

concepts.definition: Randomizing the order in which training examples are visited, by a full permutation or an approximate buffered shuffle over sharded files, trading the randomness that stochastic optimization assumes against the sequential reads that storage delivers cheaply.
concepts.label: Dataset shuffling

concepts.definition: Fitting training-specific variation that does not persist in new data, causing training performance to overstate generalization.
concepts.label: Overfitting

concepts.definition: An estimate of uncertainty in an individual prediction, sometimes decomposed into data noise and model uncertainty, used to support abstention, deferral, or data acquisition.
concepts.label: Predictive uncertainty estimation

concepts.definition: The probability that an experiment detects an effect of a stated size, fixed by sample size, outcome variance, and the significance level, which decides how much traffic or how many evaluation items a comparison needs before its answer can be trusted.
concepts.label: Statistical power

concepts.definition: Measures of a retriever's ranked results against relevance judgments, such as recall at k, mean reciprocal rank, and normalized discounted cumulative gain, which show the retrieval depth and ranking quality a downstream reranker or generator can rely on.
concepts.label: Retrieval quality metrics

concepts.definition: Generating candidate responses, filtering them with an acceptance criterion, and fine-tuning on accepted responses to turn a selection signal into supervised training data, with repeated filtering potentially reducing diversity.
concepts.label: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning

concepts.definition: Ending training according to a held-out validation criterion and selecting a checkpoint under that criterion, limiting additional compute and potentially reducing overfitting.
concepts.label: Early stopping

concepts.definition: Training to minimize the highest expected loss among predefined groups so that poor subgroup performance is not hidden by average loss.
concepts.label: Group distributionally robust optimization

concepts.definition: The fixed scheme of role markers and special tokens that serializes system instructions, user and assistant turns, and tool calls into one token sequence, which must match between fine-tuning and serving or the model misreads turn boundaries.
concepts.label: Chat template

concepts.definition: Rules that terminate autoregressive generation when a stopping criterion is met, including an end token, a stop sequence, or an output-token limit.
concepts.label: Stop conditions and output-length limits

concepts.definition: A written or automated procedure attached to an alert that says how to confirm, mitigate, and escalate a known failure, so that response speed does not depend on who is on call.
concepts.label: Runbook

concepts.definition: Whether rollout generation and policy updates share the same accelerators, alternating phases and re-sharding weights in place, or run on separate pools that exchange weights and samples, trading idle time within each phase against transfer cost and policy staleness.
concepts.label: Colocated versus disaggregated RL post-training

concepts.definition: Refining an answer through successive model calls conditioned on earlier drafts and internal or external feedback, spending additional inference compute on dependent revisions.
concepts.label: Sequential revision

concepts.definition: Learning from a small labeled set together with a large unlabeled one, typically by training on confident model predictions for unlabeled examples or by enforcing consistent predictions under perturbation, which lowers labeling cost but can reinforce the model's own early mistakes.
concepts.label: Semi-supervised learning

concepts.definition: A self-supervised or paired-data objective that pulls representations of matched views or pairs together and pushes mismatched ones apart, whose quality depends on how many negatives each step sees, which makes large batches and their memory a systems cost.
concepts.label: Contrastive learning

concepts.definition: Approximating a training step's accelerator memory as a per-parameter cost for weights, gradients, and optimizer state in their chosen precisions, plus activation memory that grows with batch size, sequence length, and depth, to decide what fits before a run is launched.
concepts.label: Training memory estimate

concepts.definition: A declared bound on cumulative privacy loss across releases involving overlapping individuals, tracked through composition accounting to constrain further releases.
concepts.label: Privacy budget and accounting

concepts.definition: The distinct points at which disparity enters an ML system, from the world the data records, who is sampled, how labels and features are measured, pooling heterogeneous groups into one model, an unrepresentative evaluation set, and use outside the intended context, each of which calls for a different remedy.
concepts.label: Sources of bias in the pipeline

concepts.definition: Accounting for purchased-electricity emissions using grid-average emission factors or qualifying contractual instruments, which changes the emissions attributed to the same electricity consumption.
concepts.label: Location-based vs. market-based carbon accounting

concepts.definition: A caller's time limit propagated to dependencies so they can stop work after the remaining budget expires, bounding caller wait and reducing abandoned work when cancellation is enforced.
concepts.label: Timeouts and deadline propagation

concepts.definition: Law governing the collection, use, retention, and automated use of personal data, which imposes obligations such as consent, purpose limitation, deletion, impact assessment, and rights over automated decisions that an ML system must implement in its data pipeline, models, and decision flow.
concepts.label: Data protection regulation

concepts.definition: Theft of a model's parameter files from training, storage, or serving infrastructure by insiders or intruders, as distinct from reconstructing the model through its query interface, which the owner counters with access control, encryption at rest, attested execution, and egress limits.
concepts.label: Model weight theft

concepts.definition: An inventory of the datasets, base weights, libraries, and build steps that produced a model, with versions and hashes, so consumers can check every component against vulnerability and trust lists before depending on the model.
concepts.label: AI bill of materials

concepts.definition: Recording and disclosing harms and near-misses caused by a deployed AI system to an internal register or an external authority or database, as regulation or policy requires, so that patterns across deployments feed back into risk management.
concepts.label: AI incident reporting

concepts.definition: Investigating how a network's internal representations and computations produce behavior through analysis and interventions, to test explanations at the level of internal components.
concepts.label: Mechanistic interpretability

concepts.definition: An independent assessment that a system meets specified safety requirements for a stated use, providing evidence for deployment approval and review of relevant changes.
concepts.label: Safety certification

concepts.definition: Criteria used to judge whether residual risk is acceptable or tolerable in a stated application and whether additional risk reduction is required.
concepts.label: Risk acceptance criteria

concepts.definition: Periodically running test workloads with known outputs on fleet accelerators and processors, at intake and during production, to find defective or silently miscomputing units before they corrupt jobs, at the cost of fleet time spent on tests.
concepts.label: Fleet hardware screening tests

concepts.definition: On-chip event counters, such as cycles, issued instructions, cache misses, bytes moved, and active compute units, that profilers sample to compute achieved bandwidth and arithmetic rate and to attribute stalls to their cause rather than to elapsed time alone.
concepts.label: Hardware performance counters

concepts.definition: An append-only harness-owned record of intents before dispatch and outcomes after execution, together with approvals and budget state, that supports recovery, replay, evaluation, and audit.
concepts.label: Trajectory log

concepts.definition: Estimating a platform's pose change by integrating its own motion measurements, from wheel encoders, inertial units, or feature motion in camera and lidar frames, whose error grows without bound with distance traveled unless corrected by loop closure or an external reference.
concepts.label: Odometry and dead reckoning

concepts.definition: The time or interval over which a measurement is acquired, whose spread across rows or beams can require motion compensation before observations are fused.
concepts.label: Capture timing and rolling shutter

concepts.definition: Variation in the period or completion time of a periodic sensing, inference, or control task, which degrades a controller designed for a fixed sample interval even when every deadline is met, so real-time budgets bound the spread of completion times and not only their worst case.
concepts.label: Timing jitter

concepts.definition: A device network engineered to provide bounded delivery under stated traffic and scheduling assumptions, whose cycle time and occupancy constrain sensing and control deadlines.
concepts.label: Real-time fieldbus

concepts.definition: The allowed gain or phase variation before a specified feedback loop becomes unstable, used to budget delay and model uncertainty around an operating point.
concepts.label: Loop stability margin

concepts.definition: Feedback control that regulates the relationship between motion and contact force, by commanding a virtual stiffness and damping or by tracking a force setpoint, so a robot can touch, push, and insert without the force spikes that pure position control produces at contact.
concepts.label: Impedance and force control

concepts.definition: An external action whose outcome is unknown after dispatch, requiring reconciliation or retry-safe endpoint semantics before recovery chooses whether to repeat or skip it.
concepts.label: In-doubt action

concepts.definition: Model-required bytes of weights and KV cache per decoding step divided by step time and by the aggregate peak memory bandwidth of the participating devices, the memory-bound counterpart of model FLOPs utilization, stated for a given batch and cache configuration.
concepts.label: Model bandwidth utilization

concepts.definition: Idle, pre-provisioned accelerators or nodes reserved to replace failed workers, reducing the delay of acquiring replacement resources at the cost of reserved capacity.
concepts.label: Hot-spare capacity

concepts.definition: Planning one training job across accelerators in several datacenters by placing the low-communication parallelism dimension (pipeline stages, local-SGD replicas, or asynchronous hierarchies) on the long, narrow inter-site links and the bandwidth-hungry dimensions inside each site, and scheduling the WAN transfers against its latency and bandwidth.
concepts.label: Geo-distributed training

concepts.definition: Separating privileged planning from an unprivileged model that parses untrusted content, so that parsed values reach the planner only as references and a trusted runtime, often with provenance tracking, checks derived values before tool execution.
concepts.label: Quarantined-model pattern

concepts.definition: Measuring how often a model abandons a correct answer or endorses a user's mistaken claim under pushback, authority cues, or social pressure, usually across several turns, so that agreement-seeking is measured separately from task accuracy.
concepts.label: Sycophancy evaluation

concepts.definition: The bytes a parallel plan must exchange per unit of local arithmetic, which, set against link bandwidth and the accelerator's FLOP rate, says whether a stage is communication-bound in the same way arithmetic intensity says whether a kernel is memory-bound.
concepts.label: Communication-to-computation ratio

concepts.definition: The historical trends by which transistor density doubled on a steady cadence while, for a long period, power density stayed constant as transistors shrank; the end of constant power density is why added transistors can no longer all be clocked at once, pushing designs toward parallelism and specialization.
concepts.label: Technology scaling

concepts.definition: Applying several compression methods in a chosen sequence, whose interactions can reinforce or diminish their individual savings and must be evaluated jointly for quality and execution cost.
concepts.label: Compression technique composition

concepts.definition: Meeting a latency target under rising load by switching requests to a cheaper variant of the same model, such as a lower-precision copy, a pruned subnetwork, or fewer layers, so capacity is bought with controlled quality loss instead of queueing or rejection.
concepts.label: Fidelity-adaptive serving

concepts.definition: Overlapping stages of a compound ML application by streaming intermediate results to downstream stages as their dependencies become available, reducing critical-path latency while preserving dependency order.
concepts.label: Compound workflow pipelining

concepts.definition: Computing the set of states a system, or another agent in its workspace, can reach within a time horizon under its dynamics and bounded inputs or disturbances, used to prove a safe set invariant, to size clearance margins, and to screen proposed motions against where other agents could be.
concepts.label: Reachability analysis

concepts.definition: Tracking group fairness metrics on production traffic over time, with the sampling, delayed-label, and protected-attribute availability problems that make subgroup estimates noisier than aggregate ones, so that disparities introduced by drift or retraining are caught before they accumulate.
concepts.label: Fairness monitoring

concepts.definition: Physical-link degradation that produces excessive bit errors, retraining, or intermittent disconnections, causing retransmission and communication stalls when protection mechanisms cannot absorb it.
concepts.label: Link signal degradation and flaps

concepts.definition: The elementwise or gated nonlinearity applied between a network's linear layers, whose choice sets whether activations contain exact zeros, whether a block needs an extra gating projection, and how cheaply the operation fuses into the preceding matrix multiply.
concepts.label: Activation function

concepts.definition: Running attention layers and the feed-forward or expert layers on separate accelerator pools during decode, so memory-bound attention over the KV cache and compute-bound expert matmuls are each batched and provisioned on hardware suited to them, at the cost of streaming activations between pools at every layer.
concepts.label: Attention-FFN disaggregation

concepts.definition: Estimating deployment class priors from unlabeled predictions under stable class-conditional input distributions and adjusting weights or probabilities to reduce errors from the changed priors.
concepts.label: Label-shift estimation and prior correction

concepts.definition: The data structure a robot keeps of its environment, such as an occupancy grid, signed-distance field, point cloud, mesh, or semantic layer, chosen by the queries that planning and collision checking must answer at their rates and by the memory and update cost the onboard computer can afford.
concepts.label: Map representation

concepts.definition: Estimating accelerator time from workload demand and effective hardware performance, then applying resource prices to estimate monetary compute cost under a stated deployment plan.
concepts.label: Compute cost estimate

concepts.definition: Classifier metrics that separate the two error types, false positives and false negatives, and the curves (ROC, precision-recall) that show how a decision threshold trades them, which matter whenever classes are imbalanced or the two errors cost differently.
concepts.label: Precision, recall, and ROC analysis

concepts.definition: Giving instructions from the system, the user, and retrieved or tool-returned content distinct privilege levels, through prompt formatting, delimiting, or training, so that lower-privilege content is less able to override higher-privilege instructions.
concepts.label: Instruction privilege levels

concepts.definition: Reconfiguring distributed training around surviving replicas of model and optimizer state so that the job resumes after supported worker failures without a full-job restart or durable-checkpoint reload, reducing recovery delay at the cost of redundancy and reconfiguration.
concepts.label: Restart-free failure recovery

concepts.definition: Serialization of a shared-memory request when threads access different addresses in the same bank, reducing effective shared-memory bandwidth.
concepts.label: Shared-memory bank conflict
